newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian shares jump, technical problems persist.
newsitem.headline: Belgian shares jump, technical problems persist.

text.p: Belgian shares opened stronger after the Dow Jones roared ahead overnight, but dealers noted little follow through buying and some persistant technical problems with bourse price information.

The start of trading, normally at 0800 GMT, was delayed by thirty minutes due to a technical hitch at the bourse, but 15 minutes later some dealers were still experiencing difficulties. "I can't see prices or volumes," one noted.
A bourse official said a few traders were having problems receiving the price information feed, but were still able to trade.
By 0900 GMT the Bel-20 index of leading shares had risen to 2,219.54 points, 23.11 points or 1.05 percent above the previous close and up from an opening level of 2,212.95.

A stronger dollar, lower bond market yields and rising stock markets across Europe all gave support. But with a new forward market account starting on Thursday players would be reluctant to open new positions today, dealers noted.

Construction firm Franki which published annual results late Tuesday was an early loser, shedding 4.1 percent to 470 francs. Franki announced its 1996 group loss narrowed to 110 million francs from 138 million in 1995, but still no dividend.

"(The loss) is not that bad if we take into account 140 million francs of exceptional charges...," Generale Bank said in its daily market commentary, adding it maintained its "hold" rating on the stock due to a progressive renewal of interest for the building sector in Europe.

Chemicals stock Solvay was the most heavily traded stock in value terms, up 1.6 percent at 20,775 francs with 4,210 shares traded. Bank Degroof's research department said the share was attratively priced versus its European peers and was a ""buy". Profit growth would be driven by plastics, though the picture was less rosy for 1998 and beyond, it said.

Degroof also expected more gains from insurer Fortis, which stood 1.75 percent higher at 6,390 francs. "Fortis AG's 1997 price to earnings ratio (14.3) remains interesting compared with a European sector average of 17.3, it said, adding the share was still undervalued in the longer term.
The only Bel-20 stocks lingering in the red were oil major Petrofina, down 1.0 percent at 12,625 francs, and shipper CMB, down 0.77 percent at 2,580 francs.
CMB has been depressed by details of its final 1996 results which were published at the weekend, as well as by dollar weakness in previous sessions.
